tagline: OV-105 — fifth Shuttle, built from spares to replace Challenger. First Hubble servicing STS-61 (1993); delivered Unity + Canadarm2
dispatch: Endeavour, OV-105, was the last orbiter built — assembled from structural spares to replace Challenger, so that even the fleet's newest member carried the memory of its worst day. It flew the first Hubble servicing mission, STS-61, the flight that corrected the telescope's flawed mirror and rescued the observatory's reputation, and it did heavy lifting in the assembly of the International Space Station. It was the youngest of the fleet and among the busiest, flying until the program's final years.
description: Fifth and last operational orbiter, built from structural spares after Challenger left NASA with only three flight-rated orbiters. Named via a national schools competition after Captain Cook's HMS Endeavour. First flight STS-49 (1992-05-07) included the first three-person EVA (to capture the stranded Intelsat VI satellite). Highlights: STS-61 (1993-12) first Hubble servicing restored Hubble's optics; STS-88 (1998-12-04) first ISS assembly flight delivering Node 1 Unity; STS-100 (2001-04) installed Canadarm2; STS-130 (2010-02) installed Tranquility + Cupola; STS-134 (2011-05) installed the AMS-02 cosmic-ray detector — final EVA crew of the Shuttle programme. On display at the California Science Center, Los Angeles.
best_known_for: Youngest Shuttle; first Hubble servicing (STS-61); delivered Unity + Canadarm2 + Tranquility / Cupola
